Nasice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Našice, Croatia

Not demolished. Wealthy members of Našice's Jewish community, organized by the end of the 19th century, played a significant role in the town's economic development; the population reached 599 (6.5 percent of the town) in 1910. After the Nazi invasion of Yugoslavia, the entire Jewish community was deported to and killed in death camps, and the synagogue was destroyed in 1942. This cemetery, established in 1805, holds 203 graves and nearly 70 identified tombstones, the oldest dated 1835 and the latest 1941.
